games.name: Don't Starve
games.intro: Don't Starve is a real-time survival and crafting game. A trial starts Wilson in an undeveloped first-day base-game world with DLC disabled and the official Long Day option, retaining a day/dusk/night cycle. This setting measures early continuous survival and ordinary resource, crafting, building and food progress rather than Adventure Mode completion. Surviving time is never pooled across deaths.
games.controls: W/A/S/D move. Space performs a nearby contextual action. F attacks a nearby target. Left click performs the primary action at the pointer. Right click performs the secondary action at the pointer. Pointer hover reveals native action labels, and dragging moves an object to a selected destination. Escape opens or closes menus, Tab toggles the map, Q/E rotate the camera, and Return confirms menu selections. Scroll changes zoom or scrolls the visible interface. These are ordinary input bindings, not a strategy. Number keys 1 through 9 and 0 activate the native action for items in inventory slots 1 through 10. The native mouse-operated crafting bar uses left clicks to toggle category tabs and pointer hover to select entries; clicking an entry or its native button activates it. The separate keyboard-operated crafting panel uses W/S to select a category, A/D to select an entry, and Space to activate the current selection. In that keyboard panel, a mouse click activates the current selection; moving the pointer does not select another entry.
games.case: GPT-6-Astra in frozen execution earns 31 milestones in 229 decisions before its first native death at two hours. Gathering and crafting milestones arrive early: twigs in the first minutes, a torch and berries by 40 minutes and a pickaxe by 45 minutes. The survival ladder then adds a milestone for every further 48 seconds of native age, up to 672 seconds, together with collection milestones such as cut reeds.

games.name: Oxygen Not Included
games.intro: Oxygen Not Included is a real-time colony-management game. Duplicants carry out reachable queued jobs according to native priorities while consuming resources. The standard Survival prepared start uses the base game, Terra and three duplicants at cycle zero. Colony development includes construction, resource production, research and space exploration. The game has native pause and speed controls.
games.controls: Use left click to select objects and interface buttons, right click or Escape to cancel, and hover to inspect tooltips. Drag with the left button to apply an active area tool across multiple tiles. G selects Dig. WASD pans the camera; the wheel zooms. Space toggles native pause and Tab cycles through the three simulation speeds. Tool and menu state can change key behavior.
games.case: GPT-6-Astra in live execution builds the colony's basic infrastructure in the first hour: an outhouse, a ladder and an oxygen diffuser at 14 minutes, a manual generator, wire and the first produced power at 30 minutes, and a pitcher pump, a battery and the first produced food at 62 minutes. It earns 19 milestones over 635 decisions and runs to the end of its budget.

games.name: art of rally
games.intro: A top-down rally driving game. The run opens at the beginning of a custom rally. Driving stages alternate with result and continuation screens, ending at the final rally result.
games.controls: W is throttle, S is brake/reverse, A and D steer left and right, and Space is the handbrake. Enter confirms the displayed menu or result selection. The car uses automatic transmission. The driving-only preparation disables in-race pause, manual recovery and restart; automatic recovery and result navigation remain available.
games.case: DeepSeek-Flash in live execution makes 1747 decisions, the most of any art of rally trial, and keeps the car on the road through stage 1 and beyond. Checkpoints arrive steadily over the whole budget, from the first stage-1 checkpoint after one minute to the fifth checkpoint of stage 4 near the end of the third hour, for 18 milestones.

games.name: The Binding of Isaac
games.intro: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance is a single-player top-down roguelike shooter. You play Isaac on Normal difficulty in a fixed-seed run. Each floor is a grid of rooms seen from above; entering a room with enemies closes its doors until every enemy is dead. Each floor has one boss room, and defeating its boss opens a trapdoor to the next floor. Floors 1 and 2 are the Basement, 3 and 4 the Caves and 5 and 6 the Depths (alternate variants of these floors exist). Mom is the boss of floor 6; defeating her ends the run with the ending. Health is shown as hearts at the top left; losing all of them ends the run, and the game then restarts from the same seed. The run starts in the start room of floor 1 with three red hearts and no items.
games.controls: Keyboard only. W, A, S and D walk up, left, down and right, and can be combined for diagonals. The arrow keys fire tears in that direction while held. E places a bomb, Space uses the active item and Q uses a held pill or card. Items and pickups are collected by walking over them, and doors and trapdoors are used by walking into them.
games.case: GPT-6-Astra in frozen execution leaves the start room within a minute, clears rooms and visits the shop on floor 1, and reaches floor 3 after 109 minutes. Collectibles and room counts accompany the floor milestones; the trial ends with Isaac's death after two hours, with 16 milestones.

games.name: Papers, Please
games.intro: Papers, Please is a document inspection simulation played through consecutive workdays. You operate a border checkpoint, examine travelers and their documents, and make admission decisions through the visible interface. Workdays have a running clock, and the story can conclude in different endings. This run begins in the first workday office with a fresh English normal-difficulty story profile and no travelers processed.
games.controls: Use the mouse to click visible interface controls and to drag documents and other movable objects between screen positions. The left mouse button selects, presses, picks up and releases objects. Consult the visible game interface for available controls.
games.case: GPT-6-Astra in frozen execution processes its first five entrants after 21 minutes and ten after 49 minutes, with ten correct decisions. It reaches day 2 at 67 minutes and has made 25 correct decisions, including ten denials, at 142 minutes.

games.name: Left 4 Dead 2
games.intro: Left 4 Dead 2 is a first-person cooperative shooter. Four survivors, one of them controlled by you and three by the computer, fight through hordes of infected and special infected. This benchmark covers the first chapter of the Dead Center campaign, the hotel, on Easy difficulty. The run starts on the hotel rooftop in a fresh campaign. The route leads down through the hotel to an elevator and then through the ground floor to a safe room whose door closes behind the team and loads the next map; the run ends when that happens. A survivor who falls can be revived or healed by teammates.
games.controls: W, A, S, D move. Left and Right arrow keys turn the view; Up and Down arrow keys look up and down. J fires the equipped weapon (hold for automatic fire). K shoves nearby enemies. E uses or picks up objects, opens doors and presses buttons. R reloads. Space jumps and Left Control crouches. Keys 1 to 5 select the weapon slots (primary, secondary, grenade, health item, pills or adrenaline). Escape opens the pause menu.
games.case: DeepSeek-Flash in frozen execution advances along the chapter route in steps of three percent. It covers 21% of the route in the first half hour, stays alive for ten minutes after the first 9%, and is verified from 27% to 48% of the route at 169 minutes, for 21 milestones over 1977 decisions.

games.name: Stardew Valley
games.intro: Stardew Valley is a farming and life simulation. You play a farmer who has inherited a run-down farm next to Pelican Town. Each in-game day runs from 6:00 am to 2:00 am, about fourteen real minutes outside menus; sleeping in bed ends the day and saves the game, and staying up past 2:00 am or running out of energy makes the farmer pass out. Days pass through four 28-day seasons. Crops are planted, watered and harvested on the farm; items can be sold, and the town has shops, villagers, a beach, a river, a forest and the mines. The long-term goal is restoring the abandoned Community Center in town: its six rooms are restored by completing bundles, which are sets of specific items donated at the room's Junimo scroll, and the Center is restored when every room is complete. The run starts inside the farmhouse on Year 1, Spring 2 at 6:00 am with 500 gold, the starting tools and a 12-slot backpack. To make progress toward restoring the Center, prioritize these scored steps: harvest a crop, catch a fish, find copper ore, earn 1,000 gold, learn to read Junimo text, complete one bundle, complete three bundles, restore one room, restore three rooms, and restore all six rooms.
games.controls: W, A, S and D move the farmer. C uses the selected tool or item; X checks, talks to or interacts with what the farmer faces, and confirms dialogue. The number keys 1 to 0 select toolbar slots. E or Escape opens and closes the inventory and game menu, F the quest journal and M the map. In menus, shops and dialogue choices, the left mouse button clicks buttons and items.
games.case: GPT-6-Astra in frozen execution plays for an hour and a half before its first milestone is verified. It then visits the bus stop, the town and the beach, reaches the mountain, makes its first cast, and has met fifteen villagers by the end of the budget, for 13 milestones.

games.name: Untitled Goose Game
games.intro: Untitled Goose Game is a real-time puzzle game in a fixed village. You control a goose through the garden, high street, back gardens and pub, then reach the model village, take its bell and return the bell to the starting area to finish the game. The run starts from a new game at the title screen with no completed tasks.
games.controls: Left-click a visible destination to walk there; clicking farther away keeps the goose moving toward that point. Move the mouse to aim the head. The right mouse button uses the beak. Hold Control to bend the neck. Space honks, X flaps the wings and Tab shows the task list.
games.case: GPT-6-Astra in frozen execution spends two hours in the opening areas before entering the garden, then completes its first to-do task, making the groundskeeper wet, 41 minutes later. Moments (1) and (2) show the trial before its first milestone.

games.name: Factorio
games.intro: Factorio is a single-player factory construction and survival game. The base-game freeplay ending is the first rocket launch from Nauvis. The character can gather materials, craft items, place buildings and use research. Production and enemies advance continuously. The trial starts at the ordinary character spawn on a fixed seed 12345 Death world marathon map, before player mining, building or research. Space Age and gameplay mods are disabled. Native character death ends an attempt.
games.controls: WASD moves the character. Point at a world object and hold J to mine it; mining is rebound from the right mouse button so both model forms can hold it. Left-click interacts with objects, inventory slots, crafting recipes and buttons, or places the held entity. Right-click splits stacks in menus. E opens the inventory and crafting panel. T opens research. Q clears the cursor or selects a matching held object. R rotates a held entity. F picks up nearby items. Space fires at enemies. Number keys select quickbar slots. M opens the map. Escape closes an open panel or opens the menu. The mouse wheel changes zoom. These controls are identical in live and frozen modes.
games.case: GPT-6-Astra in frozen execution earns 50 milestones, the most of any trial outside PEAK and Understand. It mines its first iron ore at 8 minutes, places a new furnace and smelts its first iron plates by 15 minutes, produces copper plates at 71 minutes and reaches 100 iron plates near the end of the budget.

games.name: Hollow Knight: Silksong
games.intro: Hollow Knight: Silksong is a 2D action platformer. You play Hornet in the kingdom of Pharloom, a world of connected rooms with enemies, hazards and bosses, and gain abilities that open further paths. Act one climbs through many regions toward the Citadel at the top of Pharloom; act two takes place in and around the Citadel and ends with an ending sequence. Hornet has a row of masks as health and a silk spool that fills by hitting enemies; silk can be spent to bind, which restores masks. Resting at a bench restores health and sets the respawn point. When Hornet dies she respawns at the last bench she rested at, or at the starting point of Moss Grotto before she has rested at one, and leaves a cocoon where she fell; the game continues rather than restarting. The run starts in normal mode, the only mode available at the start, in Moss Grotto, the opening area, with full health and no enemy killed yet.
games.controls: Arrow keys move. Up or Down, pressed without Left or Right, interacts, for example to talk or to sit on a bench. Z jumps (hold for a higher jump). X attacks with the needle. C dashes once Hornet has that ability; it is not available at the start. A binds. Escape opens the pause menu. In menus, arrow keys select and Z confirms.
games.case: GPT-6-Astra in frozen execution explores the opening area for almost two hours before it finds the way out. Leaving the opening room and entering Moss Grotto are verified together at 115 minutes, and the trial ends in a native death shortly afterwards.

games.name: PEAK
games.intro: PEAK is a first-person climbing survival game. A fresh attempt begins at the title screen, continues through an airport and then an island expedition. Ascending through successive regions leads toward the summit. An expedition can end in native victory or loss. The island rotates daily.
games.controls: WASD moves; Shift sprints or leaps while climbing; Space jumps; Control crouches; E interacts; Q drops or throws (hold); 1-3 selects item slots, 4 selects the backpack, and Tab stashes the selected item. The mouse turns the view or operates menus; left mouse climbs or uses an item, right mouse offers a helping hand or alternate item use. Escape opens the menu. When fully downed, hold the interaction key E to give up. Shared aliases: arrow keys move the mouse at 600 pixels per second; J and K hold left and right mouse respectively. Native free mouse and keyboard actions remain available to the language model.
games.case: GPT-6-Astra in frozen execution climbs 76 meters in 615 decisions, the most milestones of any trial. The ascent begins after 22 minutes and proceeds in bursts: three to 22 meters by 41 minutes, 29 to 53 meters by 64 minutes, and 63 to 76 meters by 74 minutes. Every height milestone above 76 meters is a frontier milestone.

games.name: Slay the Spire
games.intro: Slay the Spire is a single-player deck-building roguelike. You play the Ironclad on Ascension 10 and climb three acts of a branching map, choosing rooms (ordinary fights, elites, rest sites, shops, events, treasure). Fights are turn based: each turn you get energy and a hand of cards, play attacks and blocks against enemies whose next move is shown above them, then end the turn. After fights you add cards, relics and potions. Each act ends with a boss on floor 16, 33 and 50; dying ends the run. The run starts on floor 1 of a fixed-seed Ascension 10 run, right after the opening fight, with 72 of 80 HP and the Ascender's Bane curse in the deck.
games.controls: Mouse only for almost everything: click a card then click or drag it onto a target, click map nodes to travel, click rewards and buttons. Hovering shows card and relic details. E ends the turn. Escape opens or closes menus and overlays.
games.case: GPT-6-Astra in live execution climbs Act 1 over the whole budget: floors 2 and 3 and the first event within minutes, a 13-card deck by 20 minutes, a rare card on floor 6 at 48 minutes, and the Act 1 boss with three upgraded cards at 138 minutes, for 34 milestones.

games.name: Civilization VI
games.intro: Civilization VI is a turn-based empire-building game. This local run uses Standard Rules, an Ancient Era Aztec start under Montezuma, Prince difficulty and one AI opponent. Only Science Victory is enabled. The free Aztec Civilization Pack is the only enabled additional content; expansion rules and community mods are disabled. Defeat occurs if the human civilization is eliminated or another team wins. Gameplay starts from a fixed undeveloped save after one documented preparation turn.
games.controls: Use left clicks to select units, cities, menu entries and map tiles. Right clicks issue map orders for a selected unit. M selects the move command, which can then be targeted with a left click. The arrow keys pan the map. The configured input profile supplies ordinary keyboard and pointer controls, using fixed points or native Box targets as declared by that profile. Units, research and production choices use the game's visible controls. The game waits for player input between turns; no process pause is used.
games.case: DeepSeek-Flash in live execution founds its city at once and develops it over 1806 decisions: astrology and a builder at 14 minutes, horseback riding and a granary at 43 minutes, and construction at 175 minutes, for 23 milestones.

games.name: Baba Is You
games.intro: Baba Is You is a turn-based puzzle game. Each level is a grid of objects and word tiles; rows or columns of words such as BABA IS YOU or FLAG IS WIN form the rules that are currently true. Pushing word tiles changes the rules, for example making a wall passable or a different object the winner. You clear a level by reaching an object that is WIN while you control something that is YOU. Levels sit on world maps: clearing levels opens paths to more levels and new areas, and the game ends after the final level of the main route. The run starts from a fresh save on the opening level.
games.controls: Arrow keys move (one tile per press). Z undoes the last move, R restarts the level, Space waits a turn, Return selects a level on the map and Escape opens the menu.
games.case: GPT-6-Astra in live execution clears the opening levels within 20 minutes and keeps solving levels for the rest of the budget, reaching five lake levels at 167 minutes, for 22 milestones.

games.name: Understand
games.intro: Understand is a single-player line puzzle game organized into numbered puzzle groups on a map. A run progresses by completing groups, revealing neighboring groups and eventually reaching the ending puzzle. The run starts at the original opening menu with three empty native save slots, using slot 1. The game has no selected difficulty modifier.
games.controls: Mouse clicks choose menu entries. A left press starts a path when no path is active; pointer motion extends the active path even after the button is released. The next left press submits that path. A left-button drag presses, moves straight and releases, so it submits an already-active path before moving. Controls include left click, pointer movement without a button and straight left-button drag. Coordinates cover the whole game window.
games.case: GPT-6-Astra in live execution solves the first panels of world 1 within 13 minutes and keeps solving panels until the last minutes of its budget, ending with panel 2-8-4. Its 62 milestones are the most of any trial outside PEAK.

abstract: Computer-use agents (CUAs) are predominantly evaluated on static productivity interfaces that wait passively for each action, leaving open how well they operate in continuous, dynamic environments closer to physical-world tasks. Commercial video games offer a compelling testbed for bridging this gap: they evolve asynchronously while an agent deliberates, and tightly integrate perception, long-horizon planning, causal reasoning, and low-level control within persistent worlds. However, evaluating CUAs in such environments requires distinguishing genuine, persistent progress from surface-level interface activity, accounting for state changes during model inference, and mitigating pretraining data contamination from static, older titles. We introduce GameCUA, a live-updating benchmark currently spanning 15 commercial games that evaluates sustained visual agent progress through native game evidence while continuously onboarding newly released titles. Agents interact purely via screenshots and ordinary keyboard and mouse inputs, without privileged state access or game-specific action APIs. Each task pairs a reproducible starting snapshot and versioned milestone rubric with verification against native saves, statistics, or progression records under a single-attempt, three-hour budget, while explicitly contrasting live execution against frozen execution in supported real-time games. Evaluations across six frontier agents show that sustained game progress remains far from solved: the strongest agent, GPT-6-Astra, averages 20.9 (live) and 28.2 (frozen) points on the real-time games and 42.0 on the turn-based games, and one third of all trials earn no verified points. Real-time games prove harder than turn-based ones for most agents, and pausing the game during inference helps in some games but hurts in others. An error analysis of 88 failure events attributes the largest share to planning (33.0%) and visual perception (20.4%) errors, while real-time latency causes 26.5% of the failures in live trials.
